The video features Dr. Paramjeet Singh, identified as a Consultant Physician & Non-Invasive Cardiologist, speaking to the camera while wearing a blue medical scrub top and a black turban. He gestures with his hands as he presents "KEY POINTS" about fungal infections. These points, displayed as text on the screen, include facts that fungi are germs that can live on dead tissue and grow in warm, moist areas. Following this, the text changes to describe conditions that make someone more likely to have a fungal infection: minor skin injuries, infrequent bathing, wet skin (like from sweating), dementia, delirium, and peripheral neuropathy. These are referenced from the US National Medical Library. The screen shifts to a simplified presentation of the information under the heading "Dr.Education," accompanied by a caution that "85% of online health information is Wrong! Always Research." He continues to explain the information in his native language. The background is a plain white wall, creating a clinical, informative setting.

The video features a man who appears to be a doctor, identifiable by his blue scrub suit and stethoscope hanging around his neck. He also sports a dark blue turban, glasses, and a beard. Throughout the segment, he is sitting and actively gesturing with his hands to explain information. Text overlays appear on the screen to support his points. One overlay reads "KEY POINTS TREATMENT: Keep your skin clean and dry. Use creams that treat fungal infections. Creams that contain miconazole, clotrimazole, ketoconazole, terbinafine, or oxiconazole, or other antifungal medicine are effective in controlling ringworm." Another overlay appears with instructions: "To use this medicine: Wash and dry the area first. Apply the cream, beginning just outside the area of the rash and moving toward the center. Be sure to wash your hands and dry your hands afterward. Use the cream twice a day for 7 to 10 days. Do not use a bandage over ringworm." A disclaimer also appears, stating "85% of online health information is Wrong! Always Research" and below that "इंटरनेट पर हेल्थ की ८५% जानकारी गलत होती है! हमेशा रिसर्च करें" ("85% of health information on the internet is wrong! Always research"). Finally, a circular graphic with "Dr. Education, SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE VIDEOS" pops up. The setting is a simple, clean background with a white wall, keeping the focus on the speaker and the information being shared. The video transitions smoothly between the doctor's explanation and the supporting text overlays.
